newsitem.title: UK: British finance minister quotes Spice Girls.
newsitem.headline: British finance minister quotes Spice Girls.

text.p: British Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke quoted the Spice Girls on Monday night as he laid out his hopes for the economy ahead of a general election and said he was glad to see the back of 1980s pop icons Bros.

At an annual dinner for leading British retailers, the finance minister quoted from the hit group's first single Wannabe, which has reached number one in 31 countries, saying: "I'll tell you what I want, what I really, really want."
He then added some not quite so catchy words of his own, "healthy, sustainable growth and rising living standards for the next five years".
Prime Minister John Major's Conservatives are lagging some 20 points behind the opposition Labour Party in opinion polls with an election due in the next 60 days.
The Spice Girls are on record as being fans of former prime minister Margaret Thatcher, a Conservative like Clarke.
Warning of a return to a late-1980s boom which led to a long recession, he said: "No one wants a return to the late 1980s -- and not just because they never want to hear another Bros record."
Bros, led by blond twins Matt and Luke Goss, hit the headlines in the late 1980s with the single "When Will I Be Famous".
Another of their hits -- "Drop The Boy" -- may currently have some meaning for Major and his Conservatives.
